title: Correct tension force
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (1) must be T = Φ²/(2 μ₀ π r²).

title: Correct interaction force
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (2) must be F = ((4-√2)/(8 π μ₀)) (Φ²/l²).

title: Flux conservation reasoning
description: Important: The solution must apply flux conservation to find the uniform field B = Φ/(π r²) inside the tube.

title: Energy method for tension
description: Important: For part (1), the student should relate the tension force to the change in magnetic energy when stretching the tube, deriving T = dW/dl.

title: Magnetic charge analogy
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must use the magnetic monopole analogy or superposition, modeling the tube ends as sources of flux ±Φ.

title: Force superposition
description: Important: The final force F must be found by correctly summing (attractive and repulsive) forces between the four effective magnetic charges.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All expressions should have consistent SI units, with force in newtons.

title: Sign error in force
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the net force F is given as repulsive instead of attractive, or if the superposition signs are reversed.

title: Misapplied flux area
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the magnetic field inside the tube is calculated using an incorrect cross-sectional area (e.g., using outer radius or length).
